title: Local warmth slopes were uncertain with route and year errors in four US frog survey samples in 2001-2015
abstract: We tested whether warmer stops within a frog survey run had more recorded species after fixed site and survey controls. We used 104,240 stop visits in 10,424 ten-stop runs on 681 Northeast and Midwest US routes in 2001-2015. Four separate region and period models gave slopes from -0.015 to -0.047 recorded species per stop per 5 C. All four route and year error checks included zero. The later Midwest route-only interval was below zero, but both the year check and a nuisance-parameter error check included zero. Only 0.64-0.77 C of temperature standard deviation remained after main controls. The result is a test of an observation index, not true richness or a causal effect of warming. Selected nights, temperature error, local habitat and only seven or eight years per test limit inference. Code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction.

display.caption: Local temperature slopes for four fixed frog species. Blue: route clusters. Orange: route and year error check. Nominal 98.75 percent intervals.
